checks.note: Auth page confirms X-Auth-Token OAuth API accounts (store/app/account-level), Bearer JWT for GraphQL Storefront, and legacy-only basic auth. MCP uses OAuth 2.1 PKCE per MCP page. OAuth2, API key-style token, Bearer, Basic (legacy), Other all justified.

Quick-start page says to sign up for a free BigCommerce trial store to test API calls. Sandbox page only describes Partner Portal creation and gives no pricing, so it was a weak citation. Production plan requirement is still not verified.
API page confirms REST and GraphQL with broad coverage (catalog, orders, customers, carts, checkouts). WebSocket appears nowhere in the docs. Searches turned up only HTTP webhooks. Remove WebSocket.

MCP overview confirms an official Store Management MCP at https://api.bigcommerce.com/mcp. It is early access, needs the store owner to enable it, and uses OAuth 2.1 with PKCE. There is also a GA Storefront MCP and a docs MCP.

ready_with_caveats fits: self-serve trial store, broad REST/GraphQL API, official MCP in early access. The blocker text needs updating because the free trial store is now confirmed on a vendor page. The WebSocket claim was wrong.

corrected.one_liner: BigCommerce is a hosted SaaS e-commerce platform for building and running online stores, with catalog, cart, checkout, order, and customer management.
corrected.auth_notes: Store-level API accounts give a static access token sent in the X-Auth-Token header. App-level credentials use an OAuth grant code flow (client ID, secret, code), and each installing store gets its own token. Account-level tokens reach all stores under a parent account. Storefront GraphQL uses a BigCommerce-generated JWT as a Bearer token. Legacy HTTP basic auth only works on existing legacy accounts. The Store Management MCP uses OAuth 2.1 with PKCE.
corrected.access_notes: The quick-start page says to sign up for a free BigCommerce trial store to test API calls. A store-level API token is then created in the store control panel (Settings > Store-level API Accounts). Partner sandboxes are created via the Partner Portal. Pricing and duration of sandboxes and trials are not stated on the pages fetched. Production use needs a paid store plan (inferred, not verified). Public marketplace apps need listing review (not verified).
corrected.blocker: Trial length and terms are not stated on the vendor pages fetched. Store-level token scopes can't be edited after creation. The official Store Management MCP is early access and needs the store owner to enable it (Settings > API and MCP > MCP) and an admin to grant scopes per user.
